about: Every PostgreSQL table created by packages/db/migrations belongs to exactly one domain. The first matching rule wins. scripts/tests/table-ownership.test.mjs fails when a migration adds a table no rule names, or a rule matches nothing. Recovery rules per domain: docs/quality/state-ownership.md; record classes (durable or log): scripts/tests/record-retention.test.mjs. Each domain also names how it recovers (recovery); the test checks the kinds and that every named row exists in state-ownership.md. A domain may list tables whose recovery differs from the domain's kind (tables); the test checks each exists in the domain.

domains.workspace: Rooms, panes, layout, clipboard, tasks, events, outbox and room artifacts
domains.cli-sessions: CLI sessions, logical CLI tasks and runtimes, Codex App Server turn state, CLI maintenance
domains.browser: Pane browser sessions, control leases, handoffs, capture jobs and the Dots browser
domains.agent-runs: Space agent sessions and runs, Room Agent, managed plans, approvals, workflows, turns, swarm and tool routing state
domains.memory: Space Memory records, graph, embeddings, consolidation and commands
domains.dots: Dots, Live conversations, goals, schedules, deliverables, tools and the shared chat
domains.nous: Nous messages, notes, decisions, goals, follow-ups, plans, turns, pane board and Away
domains.copilots: Job, Mail, Marketing, Freelance, Security and Monitoring Copilots, App Studio, Design and Video panes
domains.gateway: Space Gateway accounts, keys, limits, logs, usage and pricing, providers, models, MCP and skills
domains.streaming: Streaming bot, chat, moderation, overlay, OAuth and platform state
domains.vault: Vault items, delegations, audit, nonces and protected state (server-blind ciphertext and metadata)
domains.notifications: Space notifications, push, Telegram and the Slack/Teams channels
domains.identity: Users, invites, sessions, device sessions and paired devices with the mobile channel's keys, linked SpaceApps, linked accounts, connectors, settings and the audit trail
domains.operations: Admin operations, diagnostics, analytics, health, Space Control, setup, imports, releases, reviews, source control, demo and test fixtures

recoveryKinds.reconcile-with-host: Rows are intent; a host, workflow engine or provider holds live state and must be reconciled after a restore
recoveryKinds.rebuild-from-source: Rows are derived or reconciled from files that are the source
recoveryKinds.ciphertext-only: Server-blind ciphertext; cannot be repaired server-side
recoveryKinds.disposable: Diagnostic or probe results, in-flight attempts, caches and logs pruned on a schedule; dropping them loses no data and the next check or attempt recreates them
recoveryKinds.single-use-ledger: Rows that record a credential, code or invite as used or revoked; a restore older than the row makes it usable again until it expires
recoveryKinds.history: Logs and histories pruned by age or a keep-newest count on purpose; a restore returns the backup's window, and what retention had already removed was never kept

workspace.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).
alsoSee: Rooms, panes, tasks, sessions, events and artifact metadata

pane_reports.why: Pane progress reports; the repository deletes rows older than 14 days (pane-reports-repository.ts).

task_title_attempts.why: Rate counter of title-generation attempts: rows older than a day are deleted (task-title-repository.ts) and only the last hour and minute are counted, so losing them only resets the throttle.

cli-sessions.rule: The rows record intent and status; the CLI host and the provider hold the live process and conversation. After a restore, reconcile status with the host and resume only through a recorded native identity.

codex_app_server_handshake_checks.why: Smoke-check history: the weekly cleanup (scripts/space-db-cleanup.mjs) deletes everything older than 7 days and keeps the newest row, which the UI shows as the latest result; the next check recreates it.

codex_app_server_turn_smoke_checks.why: Smoke-check history: the weekly cleanup (scripts/space-db-cleanup.mjs) deletes everything older than 7 days and keeps the newest row, which the UI shows as the latest result; the next check recreates it.

cli_maintenance_events.why: CLI maintenance event log: the weekly cleanup deletes all rows older than 7 days (scripts/space-db-cleanup.mjs); the maintenance run records in admin_operation_runs stay.

pane_cli_transcript_chunks.why: Terminal output cache: every append keeps the newest 200 chunks of its session (PANE_CLI_TRANSCRIPT_CHUNK_CAP, space-store.ts) and the API's database retention sweep deletes the chunks of sessions EXITED for 7 days (retention-sweeps.ts, on unless SPACE_ENABLE_DB_SWEEP is false). A restore returns the backup's window; resume goes through the recorded native identity, never this copy.

browser.rule: The rows record sessions, leases and handoffs; the Browser Host holds the process and profile. After a restore the next request restarts Chrome from the recorded URL and tabs; subscriptions are disposable.

agent-runs.rule: The rows record runs and missions; the workflow engine (its own databases in the same cluster) and the providers hold execution. After a restore the API sweep ends RUNNING runs whose workflow is gone as an unknown outcome (failure-matrix.md).
alsoSee: Rooms, panes, tasks, sessions, events and artifact metadata

room_agent_events.why: Room Agent monitor events; deleted after 30 days (room-agent-monitor-repository.ts). Unlike the rest of its domain they are not run state: runs and missions are in other tables.

memory.rule: Memory records, the graph's change-set journal and the consolidation and import review state exist only in PostgreSQL; a restore returns them as of the backup. The canonical memory files are a separate source (see the rows named here); only the tables listed under tables are derived or disposable.

memory_graph_embeddings.why: Vectors made from canonical memory records; rebuilt from them after a restore. Rows for deleted records are never deleted, search only filters them out (restore-and-migrations.md, memory gaps).

memory_embedding_smoke_checks.why: Embedding provider probe results (a provider counts as working after a pass within a day); the next smoke recreates them and indexing waits for it.

vault.rule: PostgreSQL holds ciphertext, public keys and metadata only; nothing server-side can read or repair an item. A restore returns the ciphertext as of the backup; the operator unlocks again and the dock re-delegates.

vault_nonces.why: Challenge, fill and request nonces with consumed_at and expires_at (replay protection). A restore older than a consumption forgets it; the nonces are short-lived, so the window is bounded by their expiry.

dots.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

nous.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

nous_goal_events.why: A goal's log; deleted after 30 days (nous-goals-repository.ts). The goal itself is a durable record in nous_goals.

nous_load_samples.why: Minute load samples; deleted after 30 days, once an hour (nous-repository.ts). Their hour and day sums in nous_load_rollups stay.

nous_decision_ledger.why: Decision ledger rows; deleted after 180 days on each new entry (nous-repository.ts).

nous_pane_summaries.why: Pane-board lines; superseded ones are deleted after 14 days with the newest per pane kept (nous-pane-summaries-repository.ts); the next board pass writes them again.

nous_file_shares.why: A pointer that shows one Agent File in the Nous app for a while (72 h by default, apps/api/src/nous/shared-files.ts); shares past expires_at are deleted on the next share and never listed, and removing one never touches the Agent File. A restore older than a removal shows that share again until it expires; Nous shares a file again when it needs to.

copilots.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

mail_copilot_sync.why: Each Gmail account's history cursor (history_id): every sync reads Gmail's history from it and stores Gmail's newer id (syncAccount, apps/api/src/mail-copilot/service.ts). After a restore the cursor is older, so the next sync reads again what came after the backup; a message whose MAIL_RECEIVED event survived is skipped. A cursor Gmail no longer keeps (about a week) answers 404 and restarts from now with a SYNC_RESET event after reading the inbox mail dated since the last sync (inboxSince), so the gap gets its items and notices once.

gateway.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

space_gateway_sticky_bindings.why: Affinity cache: which account owns a conversation, thread or prompt cache, keyed by hash; rows carry expires_at and the gateway prunes expired ones as routine (gateway-repository.ts). It records an affinity, not an account or a conversation.

provider_validation_checks.why: Smoke-check history: the weekly cleanup (scripts/space-db-cleanup.mjs) deletes everything older than 7 days and keeps the newest row, which the UI shows as the latest result; the next check recreates it.

mcp_discovery_smoke_checks.why: Smoke-check history: the weekly cleanup (scripts/space-db-cleanup.mjs) deletes everything older than 7 days and keeps the newest row, which the UI shows as the latest result; the next check recreates it.

space_gateway_anthropic_usage.why: Anthropic's cost and usage report: every sync (5 minutes, packages/gateway/src/admin/anthropic-admin.ts, only with a saved Admin API key) replaces the last 31 days in one transaction (replaceAnthropicUsage) and sets the Claude API keys' daily COST_USD values from it. After a restore the next sync rewrites that window from Anthropic; older days are the backup's only copy.

models.why: A provider's model list, replaced in full whenever that provider's validation passes (POST /api/providers/:id/validate, replaceProviderModels in space-store.ts); no field is edited by hand. After a restore, validating the provider again rewrites it from the provider.

space_gateway_usage_windows.why: Each account's latest quota windows (used percent, reset time): rewritten from the provider's usage reads and response headers (saveUsageWindows from the Codex, Claude and Antigravity usage pollers and AccountPool.recordUsage). After a restore routing sees the backup's percentages until the next poll or request of that account rewrites them; the readings themselves are kept in space_gateway_usage_history.

mcp_servers.why: Derived metadata from the configured enabled MCP servers, never hand-edited tools or approval history. A successful discovery reads every tools/list page, then recordMcpDiscoveryCatalog serializes writers and atomically upserts the complete snapshot and removes obsolete catalog rows. Failed or incomplete discovery keeps the last complete snapshot. After a restore, run the gated discovery smoke to reconcile; until then the backup catalog remains visible.

mcp_tools.why: Derived metadata from the configured enabled MCP servers, never hand-edited tools or approval history. A successful discovery reads every tools/list page, then recordMcpDiscoveryCatalog serializes writers and atomically upserts the complete snapshot and removes obsolete catalog rows. Failed or incomplete discovery keeps the last complete snapshot. After a restore, run the gated discovery smoke to reconcile; until then the backup catalog remains visible.

streaming.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

streaming_oauth_attempts.why: In-flight provider sign-ins: a row lives at most 10 minutes (CHECK on expires_at) and the repository deletes it once expired or consumed; losing one only means starting that sign-in again.

streaming_bot_activity.why: The bot's activity log, pruned to the newest 500 rows (streaming-bot-repository.ts pruneActivity); its only other reader is the replies-per-minute guardrail over the last minute (streaming-bot-service.ts), which a restore at most resets.

notifications.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

telegram_pairing_sessions.why: Pairing codes (hash only) with a status PENDING, CONFIRMED, EXPIRED or CANCELLED and a 10 minute lifetime by default; a confirmed code cannot be replayed. A restore older than the confirmation shows it PENDING again until it expires; a disconnect deletes all rows and reads their secret_version to remove the sealed bot secrets (telegram-persistence.ts), so a restore also needs the integration row and the sealed secrets to agree.

channel_events.why: Inbound Slack and Teams channel events; deleted after 48 hours (channels-repository.ts).

identity.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

session_revocations.why: Hashes of signed sessions revoked before they expired (SEC-011). A restore older than a revocation makes that session valid again until its own expiry: re-revoke what was revoked after the backup.

user_invites.why: One-time invites with accepted_at, expiry and revocation. A restore older than an acceptance or revocation makes the invite usable again: void invites issued, used or revoked after the backup.

app_device_sessions.why: Mobile device sessions and paired phones: revoked_at decides whether a paired phone connects (mobile/channel.ts checks the row at connect and every 10 s); rows go 30 days after they ended. A restore older than a revocation lets that phone connect again until it expires: revoke it again under Settings > Devices. A restore older than a pairing makes that phone pair again.

operations.rule: PostgreSQL is the only copy of these records; a restore returns them as of the backup (RPO and restore evidence: restore-and-migrations.md).

demo_oauth_attempts.why: In-flight demo provider sign-ins: each row expires after oauthAttemptTtlMs, the API deletes expired rows (and their stored verifier) whenever it starts a new attempt (demo-projects/connections.ts), and the weekly cleanup leaves them to it; losing one only means starting that sign-in again.

system_health_metric_buckets.why: Tiered metric buckets: the repository keeps 10 s buckets for 2 hours, 60 s buckets for 48 hours and 900 s buckets for 31 days and rolls finer into coarser ones; a restore returns the backup's window. (system-health-repository.ts sweep)

system_analytics_resource_buckets.why: Tiered metric buckets: the repository keeps 10 s buckets for 2 hours, 60 s buckets for 48 hours and 900 s buckets for 31 days and rolls finer into coarser ones; a restore returns the backup's window. (system-analytics-repository.ts rollup)

admin_operation_runs.why: A CLI maintenance run is QUEUED or RUNNING only while a root runner holds /run/lock/space-cli-maintenance.lock (maintenance-lock.mjs). After a killed runner, the 45 min timer stop, a host restart or a restore, the daily repair (cli-maintenance-scheduler.mjs) takes that lock and fails the CLI maintenance rows still QUEUED or RUNNING with code MAINTENANCE_INTERRUPTED before it starts (failInterruptedCliMaintenanceRuns); SPACE_RELEASE runs keep the domain's rule.

space_setup_connection_check_runs.why: A Setup connection check is RUNNING only while the API process that admitted it runs it (SetupConnectionCheckRunManager's in-memory running map). After an API restart, a deploy, a store error inside the run or a restore, the next check admission or progress replay finishes each RUNNING row that process does not run: its unfinished connections get the failed-check result (Provider failed, CHECK_EXECUTION_FAILED) and the run is COMPLETED (finishOrphanedRun, setup-connection-check-runs.ts).

demo_operations.why: A Demo Projects Salesforce and Google Sheets sync: Salesforce and the sheet hold what was written. A row is RUNNING only inside a batch of the API that claimed it, so the API's first batch after a restart, a deploy or a restore fails every RUNNING row as DEMO_OPERATION_INTERRUPTED (FAILED, or PARTIAL when a step was done) with no automatic retry, and the pane's Retry resumes it after a check (failInterruptedOperations, demo-projects/operations.ts).
